outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with an increased risk of preeclampsia, rectovaginal group B streptococcus colonization, induction of labor, cesarean section, fetal macrosomia (≥4000 g), and NICU admission, but not with preterm birth, stillbirth, or neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: This study found that obese women had a higher risk of cesarean section compared to women of normal weight.
birth_weight: Mentioned as an outcome (fetal weight ≥4000 g)
